protections: Entity values may not carry a literal '&' (one guard, two behaviours): DOCTYPE declarations whose value contains '&' are silently dropped at src/xmlparser/DocTypeReader.js:28, and the public addEntity throws for a value containing '&' and for '&' or ';' in the identifier (src/xmlparser/XMLParser.js:47-52, mirrored at src/v6/XMLParser.js:68-73).

Numeric HTML character references are bounded in width and range in v5: at most 7 decimal or 6 hex digits, and code points outside 0..0x10FFFF are returned unchanged (src/xmlparser/OrderedObjParser.js:44-45, src/xmlparser/OrderedObjParser.js:632-640).
Entity names are validated against the XML name grammar and regex-escaped before RegExp construction (src/xmlparser/DocTypeReader.js:29, src/xmlparser/DocTypeReader.js:98, src/util.js:24-27).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: htmlEntities is false by default, so a solver can assume numeric references never decode and only guard the optional block.
These values are supplied by the embedding application, not by the parsed document, so they look out of scope for a parser denial-of-service.
The only in-repo caller (src/xmlparser/XMLParser.js:35) passes values already vetted by addEntity, so the sink looks unreachable with unvetted values.
The entity value contains no '&', so the existing guard treats it as inert text and no entity reference is formed.

src/v6 is the experimental rewrite, is not exported from the package entry (src/fxp.js:10-14), and its DOCTYPE ENTITY reader throws on an undefined binding (src/v6/XmlSpecialTagsReader.js:89), so the path is not reachable today.
Same experimental-v6 dismissal; it also surfaces as a thrown RangeError rather than unbounded expansion, so it reads as a robustness bug.
The builder consumes application objects and app-supplied entity tables, never untrusted XML, so it is out of scope for a parsing denial-of-service.

masking: T6 (no entity-value filter in src/v6/EntitiesParser.js:52-62) is masked by the broken v6 DOCTYPE reader: src/v6/XmlSpecialTagsReader.js:89 calls an undefined 'source' binding, so registerEntity throws before any DOCTYPE entity can be registered; the missing filter only becomes reachable or visible once that reader is repaired.

T4 (unvalidated entity-value sink at src/xmlparser/OrderedObjParser.js:76-86) is masked today because the only in-repo caller routes values through addEntity's '&' check (src/xmlparser/XMLParser.js:35); it becomes reachable if a caller assigns the public parser.externalEntities field directly.

conflicts.what: Fixing T1 by silently dropping any DOCTYPE value that resolves to '&' satisfies the document route, but the same natural rule at the API route (T3, src/xmlparser/XMLParser.js:47) has to throw instead of drop; a shared helper that throws would change the silent-drop behaviour the DOCTYPE path's spec depends on (spec/entities_spec.js:213), and a shared helper that only drops would leave the API route accepting the value.

The T5 fix has to be a function replacement (or escaping) at the call site src/xmlparser/OrderedObjParser.js:444; the tempting shortcut of rejecting '$' inside the T1 value check (src/xmlparser/DocTypeReader.js:28) would reject legitimate entity values that contain a literal '$' while leaving the replacement-pattern effect untouched.

fairness_risks: A blanket 'no numeric character references in DOCTYPE entity values' rule contradicts the library's own documented style <!ENTITY nbsp " "> (docs/v4/5.Entities.md:8) and the live spec case at spec/entities_spec.js:187, whose asserted output at spec/entities_spec.js:213 relies on that entity being dropped today; only references that resolve to '&' may be refused.

Plain numeric character references in document text are a normal feature, including out-of-range ones that must be returned unchanged (spec/entities_spec.js:426-481); expansion limits must not reject them.

The dynamic-entity feature (spec/entities_spec.js:228-269) legitimately substitutes values such as 'writer;' that become a reference only when joined with document text (' &' to 'writer;&'); a rule that rejects values which could form a reference across the value/text boundary would break it.
Entity values containing a literal '$' (currency or template text) are legitimate; the T5 fix must change the replacement call, not refuse the value.

Refusing the whole document because a DOCTYPE value contains '&' also refuses documents that use a decimal reference to produce '&' in an entity value, which is valid XML (the style shown at docs/v4/5.Entities.md:8); the accepted-versus-refused shape has to be drawn narrowly.

design.why: T1 is the advisory anchor and costs one judgement: the guard at src/xmlparser/DocTypeReader.js:28 tests the lexical value, so it must be made resolution-aware. T3 forces the same policy onto the API producer at src/xmlparser/XMLParser.js:47, where the dismissal is that the value comes from the application rather than the document. T5 forces the solver to see that even a value with no '&' is dangerous because the value is passed straight to String.replace as a pattern (src/xmlparser/OrderedObjParser.js:444) - it survives every value-filter fix, is a how-type that MiMo misses, and its dismissal ('no & means inert text') is different from T3's. T6 forces the fix into the second implementation at src/v6/EntitiesParser.js, dismissed as experimental and unreachable. These are four edits in four areas with four different reasons to dismiss; T2 is only a sub-shape of T1's guard, T4 is masked by src/xmlparser/XMLParser.js:35, T7 rides with T6, and T8 is builder-only. That gives the widest spread of independent judgements for this code base.

unverified: Commits 910dae5be2de and bd26122c838e are not inspectable from this worktree (no git history is readable inside the pinned tree). Attributing A's fix to the literal-'&' checks rests on the dead branch at src/xmlparser/XMLParser.js:51-52 (kept after the value check was widened from equality to indexOf) and on the doc claim at docs/v4/5.Entities.md:112.

I could not construct an end-to-end nested-expansion chain in v5 by numeric '&' alone: the numeric decoders run after the DOCTYPE entity loop (src/xmlparser/OrderedObjParser.js:442-456), so a DOCTYPE value such as '&b;' renders as '&b;' only after b's replacement pass has already run. The advisory's 'numeric entity expansion' is therefore treated here as the value-level policy question (a registered value can represent '&'), and hidden tests should confirm the exact expansion shape.

src/v6/valueParsers/EntitiesParser.js is a near-identical copy of src/v6/EntitiesParser.js (same constants and methods, class declaration one line later) that nothing imports; it is treated as dead code rather than a separate fix site.

The validator's numeric-reference scan (src/validator.js:355-368) has no length bound while named references are capped at 20 characters (src/validator.js:381); it never expands entities, so it is not counted as a trap despite matching the phrase 'entity expansion limits'.

src/v6/EntitiesParser.js:42 calls reportWarning, which is neither imported nor defined in that file; this makes addExternalEntity throw a ReferenceError instead of returning, which is a robustness bug in the same area but not counted as a trap because it fails closed.
